reason: H0 only creates a fresh context and performs one xmlXPtrEval call. It never enables ctxt->cache through xmlXPathContextSetCache, so the substantially changed cache insertion, linked-list reuse, cache limits, and cache cleanup paths remain unreachable. It also does not exercise direct or compiled XPath evaluation, including repeated evaluation on one context where lastError reset and cached-object reuse matter.
evidence: H0 calls xmlXPathNewContext(doc) followed by exactly one xmlXPtrEval(BAD_CAST expr, xpctxt).
H0 never calls xmlXPathContextSetCache; S1's xmlXPathNewContext enables caching only under XP_DEFAULT_CACHE_ON, whose definition remains commented out as /* #define XP_DEFAULT_CACHE_ON */.

S1 replaces the cache representation with nodesetObjs and miscObjs linked through xmlXPathObject.stringval and adds numNodeset/numMisc accounting in xmlXPathReleaseObject and the xmlXPathCache* functions.

S1 changes xmlXPathCompiledEvalInternal and xmlXPathEval to reset ctxt->lastError, but H0 invokes neither xmlXPathCompiledEval nor xmlXPathEval and performs no repeated evaluation on the same context.
recommended_action: Extend the harness with input-selected modes that call xmlXPathContextSetCache using varied active/value/options settings, evaluate multiple expressions on the same xmlXPathContext to populate and reuse cached objects, then disable/free the cache. Add direct xmlXPathEval and compile-plus-repeated-xmlXPathCompiledEval modes alongside xmlXPtrEval.
